target_customer: Individuals and teams who schedule many meetings, sold through a Chrome extension and web calendar app
problem: Coordinating meeting times across calendars and teams is slow; Meetingbird layered group scheduling and availability sharing on top of existing calendars.
business_model: Freemium SaaS calendar and scheduling tool aimed at per seat team plans

founders.name: Paul Dornier
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as Founder/CEO and links to his later startup Alpharun. No education or employers on the pages opened.

founders.name: Henry Dornier
founders.background_notes: YC page bio says he later cofounded Alpharun. Front's announcement calls both Dornier brothers the Meetingbird co-founders.

competitors.name: x.ai
competitors.what: AI scheduling assistant that negotiates meeting times by email
competitors.traction_then: Meetingbird's Product Hunt launch thread compared the two; commenters called Meetingbird more efficient

competitors.name: Calendly
competitors.what: Booking links for one on one scheduling
competitors.traction_then: The Meetingbird founder said a number of Calendly users switched to Meetingbird Meet

technical_complexity.rationale: A Chrome extension and web calendar over Google Calendar style APIs is standard engineering for two founders; syncing and availability logic add some difficulty.

defensibility.rationale: Scheduling links and calendar overlays were easy to copy and many tools existed; no sourced data or network effect.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Calendar incumbents kept adding scheduling features; Meetingbird was bought by Front in April 2020 to add calendar features to its inbox.

market_need_then: Scheduling friction was widely felt and several funded startups (x.ai, Calendly, Doodle) addressed it in 2017; Meetingbird reported use at companies such as Uber, Shopify and Yelp on its YC page.

branding.domain_note: Used meetingbird.com, which now redirects to front.com.

identity.voice_and_tone: YC blurb used the phrase calendar with superpowers

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand itself was found; coverage was product focused and the brand was absorbed by Front.

outcome_analysis: Meetingbird launched its web calendar and Chrome extension around the August 2017 YC demo period in a crowded scheduling market and reached about 15,000 weekly active users by April 2020, when Front acquired it and the Dornier brothers joined Front. Terms were undisclosed and the standalone app was later wound down, so it reads as a product and team acquisition rather than a breakout.
notes: Company website redirects to front.com. PitchBook snippet dated the acquisition 2018-10-24 but Front's own post is dated 2020-04-17; Front's post used. Round amount and date unknown: Front names YC and Khosla Ventures as backers. A snippet claimed founders' schools (Princeton, Harvard) from a source not opened, so education left empty. A Boomerang post says the standalone app closed on December 21 (year not shown). Dealroom listing of an enterprise value is unverified and not used. Competitor funding not checked.
